properties.instruction:

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards...beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 5:07AM PST until November 26 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low
lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to 1 foot of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and
tidal waterways. Between 9.5 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted. Tide along the open coast will also be
high, but less than what was experienced Wednesday due to
reduced surf

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM PST Thursday. High tide is at 12:54
PM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with isolated closures expected.
Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata
Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this event will be
higher than normal but not quite as high as the previous near
record recording from Tuesday 11/24 at 10.16 feet.
properties.instruction:

will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.areaDesc: Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 26 at 3:03AM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
Localized moderate to significant coastal flooding is expected
for Jalama Beach and for most coastal areas from Miramar Beach
to Rincon Point. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. Conditions
will be worse west of Point Conception, including Jalama Beach
with large breaking waves of 15 to 20 feet and moderate to
significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Until noon PST today.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. There
is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock
damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of
harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greater impacts are expected west of
Point Conception, and for most coastal areas from Miramar
Beach to Rincon Point, where damaging flooding of sea water is
more likely, especially for vulnerable low-lying coastal areas
around the time of high tide including over beaches, beach
parking lots and coastal roads. For the previously mentioned
areas, significant beach erosion is expected, powerful waves
and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean
drowning and damage to coastal structures and homes at the
waters edge. Extremely high tides of around 8.0 feet will
likely peak between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of

infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.
